note: Exceptions determine when a rule that would normally apply gets overridden to N/A, or when unresolved applicability/evidence must produce REVIEW instead of a guess. Checked AFTER applicability, BEFORE evidence check. Unresolved date_role is handled separately in rules.json validation logic (type: presence_with_role), not here - it is an evidence-quality issue, not an applicability exception.

exceptions.reasoning: Country of origin is only a mandatory declaration for imported packages. Do not fail a domestic product for missing it.

If we cannot confirm whether the product is imported, do not guess. An unresolved applicability question must not silently become N/A (which would hide a possible violation) or FAIL (which could wrongly penalize a domestic product).
exceptions.status: MVP INTEGRATION DECISION (not a legal ambiguity) - the legal requirement itself (country of origin for imports) is settled; what's open is whether this MVP's pipeline attempts import-status classification at all. Confirm with Person 1 whether that's in scope, or whether this rule always REVIEWs for the demo.

exceptions.reasoning: Best before/use by is only required for commodities that may become unfit for consumption over time (Rule 6(1)(da)). Non-perishable items (e.g. steel utensils, stationery) should not be failed for lacking this.
If perishability isn't confirmed, treat it as unresolved applicability, not N/A or FAIL.
exceptions.status: MVP INTEGRATION DECISION (not a legal ambiguity) - Rule 6(1)(da)'s requirement for perishable goods is settled; what's open is whether this MVP's pipeline classifies perishability at all, or treats every product as 'unknown' (→ REVIEW). Confirm scope with Person 1/3.

exceptions.reasoning: Confirmed: unit sale price does not apply to combination/group/multi-piece packages (2023 amendment), or to food articles (FSSAI carve-out, 2023 amendment). Plausible but NOT independently confirmed this pass: RSP-equals-USP exemption, wholesale-package exemption. An earlier version of this file also claimed an e-commerce exemption for unit sale price specifically - that claim was NOT confirmed and has been removed; the confirmed e-commerce carve-out (Rule 6(10)) applies to the manufacturing-date declaration, not unit sale price. See rule's legal_reference in rules.json for full sourcing.
Applicability of unit sale price depends on package type and pricing, which may not always be determinable from the image alone. Do not guess.
exceptions.status: MVP INTEGRATION DECISION (not a legal ambiguity) - the exemption conditions confirmed this pass (combination/group/multi-piece packages, food articles) are settled by Rule 6(11) and its 2023 amendment; RSP=USP and wholesale-package exemptions remain plausible but unconfirmed. What's open is whether this MVP's pipeline classifies package type well enough to apply any of these. Confirm scope with Person 1/3.

exceptions.reasoning: Dimensions are only meaningful for specific commodity categories, not all packaged goods.
If commodity category/relevance isn't confirmed, treat as unresolved rather than guessing N/A or FAIL.
exceptions.status: MVP INTEGRATION DECISION (not a legal ambiguity) - what's open here is engineering scope (does the pipeline classify commodity category), not legal uncertainty. Note separately: PCR-R10's underlying legal basis is now partially verified (a dimensions declaration requirement, conditional on relevance, is confirmed to exist within Rule 6(1) via secondary sources) but the exact sub-clause letter is still unconfirmed - see rules.json legal_reference. That letter-level detail remains a genuine open legal-verification item, distinct from this classification-scope decision.

exceptions.condition: colocation cannot be reliably determined from available bbox/image_geometry evidence
exceptions.effect: result = REVIEW (informational only - PCR-R11 is never scored regardless of outcome)
exceptions.reasoning: PCR-R11 is experimental. When the system can't reliably assess placement, it must say so (REVIEW) rather than defaulting to PASS or FAIL. This never affects the compliance score.

not_implemented_this_mvp: Multi-component/group package special handling beyond the unit-sale-price exemption already captured above (Rule 6(5)-adjacent area)

QR/electronic declaration handling is outside this MVP's scope. This is a statement of what's unimplemented, NOT a claim that QR/electronic declarations can never legally substitute for printed declarations - actual legal applicability may depend on product/category-specific provisions (e.g. Rule 6(10) does address electronic-network declarations for e-commerce listings, though the confirmed carve-out there is narrower than a general QR-substitution allowance - see PCR-R09/R05 legal_reference notes). Do not build or claim either 'QR always works' or 'QR never works' logic without verifying the specific applicable provision.

Full sub-condition derivation for unit_sale_price applicability (wholesale vs combination vs group vs multi-piece vs RSP==USP) - MVP treats this as one upstream boolean; see PCR-R09 applicability note in rules.json

Legibility/font-size measurement against Rule 8 thresholds - MVP only collects evidence (bbox, OCR confidence, image quality) per PCR-R11; it does NOT compute an automatic legal FAIL from pixel/font size, since the exact legal measurement methodology has not been verified
